paragraphs: Friend, the Pharisees wanted a date. Jesus gave them something better: the kingdom of God "is in your midst" (Luke 17:21). Then He told His disciples not to go chasing after every "Look, there He is!" (Luke 17:23). When the Son of Man comes, it will be like lightning that "lights up the sky from one end to the other" (Luke 17:24), so nobody will need a group chat to find out.

So what do I do while I wait? I keep my ovens ready, because Jesus says the Son of Man's day will be like the days of Noah and Lot (Luke 17:26-30). Life was going on as usual, and that wasn't the problem. The problem was living like that day would never come. I'm not saying when it happens, because only the Father knows that (Matthew 24:36). My job is to keep baking and stay ready.

Then Jesus says, "Remember Lot's wife!" (Luke 17:32). He tells us not to go back for what we left behind. He also says, "Whoever tries to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life will preserve it" (Luke 17:33). I think that's the heart of it, friend. Hold Jesus tight, hold your stuff loose, and don't wear yourself out chasing rumors.
